rows.name: ? block 16x16 tile ids (level object-graphics block at prgRom 0x8C8C, entry 0)
rows.notes: What the bytes are: the four BG-pattern-table tile ids that make the 16x16 ? block. In World 1-1 (camera 93) the ? block reads nametable 1 tiles $53/$54 top row and $55/$56 bottom row, palette 3. Origin found with no reference: the level-graphics parser around CPU $88AE-$8958 computes a data pointer from a table at CPU $8B08/$8B0C (block pointers $8B10,$8BAC,$8C64,$8C8C) and then does LDA ($06),Y / STA $0344,X (PC $88FD) and LDA ($06),Y / STA $0345,X (PC $8903, prgRom 0x8FD/0x903), writing two tiles per call into the $0341+ VRAM buffer; each object type has a 4-byte entry, so the ? block graphic lives in the block at $8C8C (first entry, type byte $C0). Proof: write_memory prgRom 0x8C8C $53->$24 (ledger seq 1, reason: blank the ? block top-left), reset_emulator, then Start,Start,hold Right 150 frames to the ? block; get_tile_at_pixel at its top-left returned tile_id 36 ($24, renders $22 periwinkle) while the top-right still returned 84 ($54) - i.e. the block lost its upper-left quadrant exactly as predicted. undo_edit restored $53.

rows.name: small Mario standing-frame tile list (player pose table entry at prgRom 0x6ECF)
rows.notes: What the bytes are: the 8 sprite-pattern-table tile ids the standing small-Mario frame is built from (the top four $FC are blank padding because small Mario is drawn in the 2x4 slot layout; the visible 2x2 is $3A,$37 over $4F,$4F). In World 1-1 small Mario standing emits OAM entries at x=40/48, y=177/185/193/201 with tiles FC,FC,FC,FC,$3A,$37,$4F,$4F, sprite palette 4; that exact byte run exists only here in PRG (search_memory "3A 37 4F 4F" -> prgRom 0x6ED3). The table sits right before the player routine that starts around CPU $EEC9 (prgRom 0x6EE9: LDA $079E). Proof: write_memory prgRom 0x6ED3 (the pose entry's 5th byte, tile $3A) -> $FC (ledger seq 1, reason: blank Mario's upper-left tile), reset_emulator, Start,Start into 1-1; list_sprites then showed OAM entry 5 tile byte 252 ($FC) instead of 58 ($3A) and the screenshot showed Mario's upper-left 8x8 quarter missing. undo_edit restored $3A.
